column3: Extends the straight-course reading to the believing community and ties it to restrained opposition.
Directly restates guidance onto the straight path, independently reinforcing its durable course dimension.
Adds a communal instance of divine favor; its completion link remains provisional and broad.
Closely supports forgiveness as protection from the harmful sequel of faults.
Within the same surah, joins removal of evils to the favor-and-guidance sequence without repeating 48:2 exactly.
Pairs forgiveness, repentance, and punishment, clarifying that covering remains distinct from consequence.
Directly repeats completion of favor and adds a long, interpretive process dimension.
Supplies the immediately preceding opening that frames 48:2's stated purposes.
Connects completion of favor to practicable observance, but the exact route is provisional.
Reiterates guidance to a straight path together with mercy and favor, though less specific than earlier cards.
Adds confession as a response to fault before the request for forgiveness.
Develops guidance as sustained right alignment rather than a bare path designation.
A concise repetition of straight-path guidance; helpful but largely covered by stronger parallels.

Makes before-and-after an exhaustive account of what was advanced and deferred.

Adds the boundary of devoted servants under the authority-associated path channel.
Relates the path to recipients of favor and preserves the contrast with other courses.
Only a general forgiveness attribute; it adds no focused link to 48:2.

Distinguishes revelation's enlivening, illuminating, and guiding functions while naming the straight path.

Links creation to continuing guidance, supporting the active rather than static course reading.

Defines the straight path as an authority-held, safeguarded course.
Directly supports completion as divine refusal to leave the light incomplete.

Specifies straightness as sustained conformity to command without excess.
Advance and delay appear, but no precise forgiveness, completion, or path link is supplied.
Identifies worship as the enacted form of the straight path.
Distinguishes concealment of a matter from a request for forgiveness, refining the covering reading.

Adds fulfillment of the divine word, a broad but relevant completion parallel.

Bare straight-path wording is fully covered by more informative earlier path cards.

No exact channel or V12 route adds to the focus reading.

No supplied route connects this response to the focus's three components.

Combines pardon, covering, and mercy in a concentrated forgiveness sequence.

Links holding fast to God with being guided to a straight path.
Places forgiveness after failure and return, adding a repair-oriented setting.
Connects wrongdoing, turning, and seeking forgiveness through an intercessory relation.

Links evil, repentance, and faith with subsequent forgiveness and mercy.
Uses the straight path as a site of obstruction, supplying contrary boundary evidence for route guidance.
Shows seeking forgiveness as a condition against punishment, closely supporting protective consequence-covering.

Adds acknowledged mixed deeds and hoped-for acceptance of repentance.
Centers divine acceptance of repentance and receipt of restorative giving.
Describes a turning back after constriction, a secondary completion-through-repair parallel.
Combines seeking forgiveness and turning with an appointed temporal interval and good provision.
Reiterates the paired movement of seeking forgiveness and turning back.
Adds forgiveness after grave interpersonal wrong while suspending immediate reproach.

Contrasts the stated way with deviation and universal potential for guidance.
Connects inward turning with divine forgiveness, qualifying forgiveness by return.
Supplies an exhaustive-record horizon for deeds, relevant to the before-and-after scope.

Relates guidance with doing good, prayer, and almsgiving as enacted forms.

Combines a divinely given way of practice with invitation to straight guidance.
Directly names an invitation to a straight path, while leaving its response open.
Places repentance and reform after wrongdoing before the forgiveness attribute.
Adds pardon and overlooking as related but distinct restorative responses.
Pairs repentance and righteous action with replacement of evils, a strong transformation parallel to forgiveness.
Restates return to God through repentance and righteous action.
Describes taking a way toward the Lord, providing a secondary route-to-destination parallel.
Directly records self-acknowledged wrong followed by a request and grant of forgiveness.

Pairs forgiveness with a great reward across a comprehensive set of faithful practices.

Directly joins acceptance of repentance with forgiveness of evils.
Links affliction to what hands have advanced while emphasizing extensive pardon.
Names divine selection and guidance to Himself, an authority-and-route parallel.
Directly identifies the addressee as being on a straight path.
Names guidance to truth and to a straight path, a close omitted path parallel.
Directly instructs the addressee to seek forgiveness for his fault, closely paralleling 48:2's addressee.
Uses the forgiveness-and-mercy attribute in the same surah's community discipline setting.
States the breadth of divine forgiveness while retaining knowledge of human development.
Combines mercy, a light for walking, and forgiveness, closely integrating guidance and forgiveness.
Pairs expiation with forgiveness and pardon, a secondary covering distinction.
Seeks forgiveness for the community and those who preceded it, adding an explicit prior-community horizon.
Repeats the completion-of-light theme in parallel to 9:32, reinforcing divine completion.
Distinguishes pardon, overlooking, and forgiveness as related protective responses.
Pairs removal of evils with magnified reward, a secondary consequence-covering parallel.
Links seeking forgiveness with a subsequent outpouring of provision.
